sn11.24:1.2: Now on that occasion two bhikkhus had a quarrel and one bhikkhu had transgressed against the other.
sn11.24:1.4: Then the former bhikkhu confessed his transgression to the other bhikkhu,
sn11.24:1.5: but the latter would not pardon him.
sn11.24:1.6: Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported to him what had happened.
sn11.24:2.1: The Blessed One said: “Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of fools:
sn11.24:2.2: one who does not see a transgression as a transgression; and one who, when another is confessing a transgression, does not pardon him in accordance with the Dhamma.
sn11.24:2.3: These are the two kinds of fools.
sn11.24:2.4: “There are, bhikkhus, two kinds of wise people:
sn11.24:2.5: one who sees a transgression as a transgression; and one who, when another is confessing a transgression, pardons him in accordance with the Dhamma.
sn11.24:2.6: These are the two kinds of wise people.
sn11.24:3.1: “Once in the past, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, instructing the Tavatiṁsa devas in the Sudhamma assembly hall, on that occasion recited this verse:
sn11.24:4.2: Do not let your friendships decay.
sn11.24:4.3: Do not blame one who is blameless;
sn11.24:4.5:
Like a mountain avalanche
Anger crushes evil people.’”
